correctness.rationale: The finite-rank length identity yields an exact deficit summed over words. A sharp scalar comparison bounds it by product-measure overlap, and an interior strictly convex Chernoff tilt gives matching root-exponential bounds. In the binary case, the exact tilted binomial identity and a uniform dominated local limit prove the n^(-1/2) phase profile. Two integrations by parts derive the beta Fourier transform, which has no zeros since Gamma has none; the p=9/10 example has an irrational phase. The seven-sample-size numerical asymptotic diagnostics corroborate, but do not establish, the general proof. Explicit assumptions, endpoints, and unproved extensions are stated in RESULT.md.

The new statement supplies the sharp Chernoff exponential rate and a nonconstant binary Fourier-periodized leading coefficient. The examined digit-remainder and stationary-digit works address different observables. Explicit residual risk concerns older equivalent singular-function arclength work; the public result-record search is non-exhaustive.

value.rationale: The finite arclength identity and known limit two leave an explicitly motivated quantitative problem. An exact Chernoff rate valid for all positive nonuniform q-ary laws, together with a sharp binary n^(-1/2) periodic prefactor proven nonconstant, isolates a previously unquantified geometry/statistics mechanism and yields a natural full-family phase classification; this is not an arbitrary numerical slice or a table recomputation.
